_comment: Curated list of project ideas that have actually been built. This is maintained by hand (the daily routine never edits it). Two entry shapes are supported: (1) a 'ref' to an existing idea by {date, n} to promote it into the Implemented section, optionally overriding fields and adding url/repo; (2) a fully standalone project. See ideas/SCHEMA.md.

projects.notes: Built in one session with zero runtime deps beyond React: verified Machado 2009 CVD matrices in linear sRGB, OKLab confusion detection, hue-preserving contrast fixes, PNG/print reports, 11 unit tests. Originally built in its own repo (pisanuw/c1) and mirrored to GitHub Pages; moved into Claude-capstone on 2026-08-27 with git subtree so history survived, with the Netlify site id pinned so the URL did not change. pisanuw/c1 is now an archived pointer and pisanuw.github.io/c1 redirects to the live app.

Built in one session: five algorithms (BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, Greedy, A*) emitting a single event trace consumed by both the canvas renderer and the narrator. Narration is rule-based instead of the suggested Claude API calls, so it is free, offline, and always matches the algorithm state. Side-by-side compare mode, RLE share links in the URL hash, seeded maze generator, 20 vitest cases. Originally built in its own repo (pisanuw/pathfinding-playground); moved into Claude-capstone on 2026-08-27 with git subtree so history survived, with the Netlify site id pinned so the URL did not change. The old repo is now an archived pointer.

Fully client-side schema explainer: paste SQL DDL, a Prisma schema, or JSON Schema and get a plain-English entity-relationship narrative, vocabulary suggestions for cryptic names, and a rule-based review of missing keys/indexes/constraints, exportable as Markdown. A hand-written parser and fixed rule set replace the idea's suggested LLM calls, so output is free, offline, and reproducible. 71 vitest tests, 88.88% coverage; lint/typecheck/build green. Deploy was blocked for 4 runs by a stale NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN repo secret; once the owner rotated it, the remaining failure was a deploy-runner bug (empty functionsDir resolved to the project root, so the CLI bundled the whole repo as functions). Fixed in deploy.mjs, deployed via GitHub Actions, and the CI runner verified the live page returns 200 and renders.

Built in one session, fully client-side: SM-2 spaced repetition drills bundled shortcut sets for VS Code, Chrome DevTools, Figma, and Vim (multi-chord sequences like Ctrl+K Ctrl+S and ciw included), plus custom JSON set upload with strict validation. Key capture derives two candidate chords per keypress (physical event.code and produced event.key), so both Ctrl+Shift+[ and Vim's $ match; browser-reserved combos (Ctrl+W/T/N) are excluded since a web page cannot capture them. localStorage replaces the suggested Supabase backend, so there are no accounts and no server. Per-tool mastery radar chart and daily streak. 78 vitest tests, 98.6% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, page verified 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: parses two versions of SQL DDL (CREATE/ALTER/INDEX, Postgres and MySQL enums) or TypeScript interfaces into a shared IR, diffs them with rename detection for tables and columns, and classifies every change safe/caution/breaking with a one-sentence migration note; exports a Markdown PR checklist. A deterministic rule set replaces the suggested Claude API calls, so verdicts are instant, offline, and reproducible. 74 vitest tests, 97% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, page verified 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: a timed bug-spotting game where 1-3 defects are planted into realistic JavaScript/Python/SQL snippets and you click the lines you would flag in review. A seeded mutation engine (11 hand-written clean templates, 51 catalogued single-line defects with title, root cause, and fix) replaces the idea's suggested Claude API generation, and a date-seeded daily challenge plus a localStorage profile (per-category accuracy radar, streaks, best score) replace the Supabase leaderboard, so rounds are deterministic, offline, and free. Scoring rewards full sweeps: 100 per defect, -25 per false flag, time bonus only when everything is found. 46 vitest tests, 99.8% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green; end-to-end flow verified in headless Chromium. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, page verified 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: a perceptual YIQ pixel diff with anti-aliasing detection (pixelmatch algorithm), grid-BFS region clustering, and a 7-type heuristic classifier (element-added/removed via local-background analysis, layout/spacing via a full-coverage displacement search, visibility via least-squares opacity fit, color via edge-map correlation, text via edge density) replace the suggested Claude Vision calls, so results are deterministic and screenshots never leave the browser. SVG overlay with filterable legend and per-region evidence, annotated PNG and standalone HTML report export, built-in sample pair covering all seven change types (verified end-to-end in headless Chromium). 56 vitest tests, 96.4% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, page verified 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side with zero runtime dependencies: a hand-written tokenizer, recursive-descent parser, three-valued-logic expression evaluator, and staged executor replay a SELECT one stage at a time (FROM, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT), showing the actual rows merging, being struck out, and collapsing into groups at every step. A deterministic narrator generated from real execution stats replaces the idea's optional Claude API narrator, and CSS animations replace Framer Motion, so explanations always match the screen and the app is free and offline. Honest SQL semantics (Kleene AND/OR, COUNT(x) vs COUNT(*), NULLs-last ordering), CSV paste with type inference, bundled demo tables and queries, URL-hash share links. 86 vitest tests, 99.7% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (runner verified the live page returns 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: a deterministic word-to-DSP lexicon (20 base sounds, 18 modifiers with synonyms) replaces the idea's suggested Claude API code generation, and a pure sample-by-sample DSP engine (swept oscillators, seeded white/pink/brown noise, ADSR envelopes, RBJ biquad filters with block-rate sweeps, feedback echo, tanh drive, bit crush, peak normalization) replaces Web Audio graphs, so the browser just plays the rendered buffer and tests assert on the exact samples the user hears. Same description always yields the same sound (seed hashed from the words); a Variation button re-rolls only the seed. Oscilloscope, per-layer signal-chain view, tuning sliders (pitch/length/brightness/echo/volume), and 16/24-bit WAV export at 22050/44100/48000 Hz. 59 vitest tests, 100% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green; UI verified end-to-end in headless Chromium. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, page verified 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: a forgiving HAR parser (skips malformed entries with warnings, wire-size fallbacks for Chrome/Firefox export quirks) feeds ten deterministic detectors (N+1 endpoint templates, cache-header audit, missing compression, redirect chains reconstructed hop by hop, serialized API waterfalls, duplicate fetches, 4xx/5xx groups, TTFB outliers, oversized payloads, HTTP/1.x connection churn) that replace the idea's suggested Claude API analysis, so reports are instant, reproducible, and the HAR never leaves the browser. Findings are ranked by severity and estimated impact, each with evidence and a copy-paste fix; SVG waterfall with phase segments, type filters, and per-finding highlighting; Markdown report export; a bundled synthetic session trips every detector. 56 vitest tests, 100% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green; verified end-to-end in headless Chromium. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow: the first run failed because package-lock.json was gitignored at the repo root and npm ci had nothing to install from; force-added the lockfile, retriggered, site created and the runner verified the live page returns 200; siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: paste code or name a concept, pick an audience (curious child, high school student, CS undergrad, non-technical adult), and get three analogies from three distinct everyday domains, each with a code-to-analogy mapping table. A curated corpus (47 concepts x 3 domains x 4 audience variants, 564 hand-written texts, ten browse groups) replaces the suggested Claude API generation, and a localStorage library with tags, search, and Markdown export replaces Supabase; read-only share links encode ids into the URL hash, so sharing needs no server. The detector combines keyword mentions with code-shape patterns and body-scoped self-call analysis (brace matching or Python indentation) for recursion; anything outside the 47 concepts gets an honest "not detected" instead of a hallucinated analogy. 125 vitest tests, 99.9% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green; UI verified end-to-end in headless Chromium. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, runner verified the page returns 200), siteId pinned afterward. Follow-up same day: audience-toggle highlight fix and an example pull-down with one test-pinned snippet per concept (47), and staged corpus expansions from 14 to 25 to 47 concepts, adding systems, language mechanics, web/networking, and software-craft topics.

Built in one session, fully client-side: the real TypeScript compiler (pinned 5.6.3) runs in a Web Worker over an in-memory file system with the full ES2022 lib.d.ts reference closure (57 files) bundled as raw text, so analysis is exact, offline, and nothing pasted leaves the browser. A post-order AST walk turns inference into a narrated story: literal types and let/const widening, generic calls showing declared signature, inferred binding (T = string, recovered defensively from internal signature state with graceful fallback), and resolved signature, unannotated callback parameters typed from context, control-flow narrowing with declared-vs-here detail, inferred return types, and compiler diagnostics threaded in right after the step where inference went astray. Hover any expression for its exact type, click to jump to its step, autoplay, major-steps filter, 8 pinned examples, URL-hash share links. The idea named no LLM, so nothing needed replacing; React was swapped for the monorepo's vanilla TS + Vite house pattern. One honest cost: the compiler-in-a-worker bundle is ~1 MB gzipped on first load. 62 vitest tests, 97.6% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green; verified end-to-end in headless Chromium. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, runner verified the page returns 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: a rule-based classifier (explicit section labels plus sentence-level cue patterns, each gene showing the evidence for its label) segments any pasted prompt into typed genes (role, persona, context, task, constraint, format, example), replacing the idea's suggested Claude API parsing; three hand-written deterministic mutations per gene type (e.g. Harden it / Soften it / Make it checkable, with case-aware word swaps like should-to-must) replace 'AI suggests three alternatives'; and a word-level LCS diff of the prompt itself replaces model-response diffing, since without API calls there are no responses to compare. A 12-rule lint scores the genome 0-100 (missing task, vague wording, brevity-vs-depth conflicts, negative-only constraints, duplicates, and more); genes can be edited, reclassified, reordered, and duplicated; a localStorage library keeps reusable genes with tags and search (replacing the implied server store); share links carry the whole genome in the URL hash; export as text, Markdown, or JSON. 87 vitest tests, 98.98% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green; verified end-to-end in headless Chromium. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, runner verified the page returns 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side with zero runtime dependencies: a hand-written five-field cron parser (names, steps, wrap-around ranges like FRI-MON, @shortcuts, vixie dom/dow union semantics), an RFC 5545 RRULE subset (FREQ/INTERVAL/BYDAY with 1MO and -1FR ordinals/BYMONTHDAY/BYMONTH/BYHOUR/BYMINUTE/COUNT/UNTIL), GitHub Actions on.schedule snippet extraction, and a deterministic rule-based English-to-cron converter that annotates every assumption and returns an honest null replace the suggested Claude API call and the cronstrue/cron-parser packages. Time-zone math builds exact offset-transition tables from the browser's IANA data (transitions binary-searched to the minute), so the dual-zone pickers convert exactly: spring-forward gap firings are reported as skipped like system cron, and ambiguous fall-back times fire once at the earlier instant. 30/90/365-day calendar heatmap with per-day fire times, plain-English schedule descriptions, next-25 table in both zones, query-param share links. 74 vitest tests, 92% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green; verified end-to-end in headless Chromium. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, runner verified the page returns 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session from a direct request: a mobile-first schedule browser for the inaugural ACM AI Leadership Summit (Hyatt Regency Atlanta, Aug 30 to Sep 2, 2026). Sticky day tabs, eleven color-coded track chips, every-term search across titles/speakers/rooms/descriptions, a starred personal agenda in localStorage, a now/next banner on the conference clock, and a one-tap toggle between Atlanta time and the viewer's own timezone (exact IANA math). The whole conference lives in one validated schedule.json, so the app doubles as a drop-in template for any conference. The build environment could not reach aisummit.acm.org (egress policy), so the bundled data is an unofficial snapshot reconstructed from ACM's public announcements, disclosed in the app footer and README. 42 vitest tests, 100% statement coverage on core logic; deploy worked first try, siteId pinned.

Built in one session, fully client-side: decomposes a pasted prompt into labeled sections (system/instructions, context, examples, user/task) by explicit label or heuristic (You are..., Q:/A: and Input:/Output: pairs), then compresses each at a light/medium/aggressive level: whitespace and filler-word removal, verbose-phrase simplification (in order to -> to, due to the fact that -> because, ...), cross-section duplicate-instruction removal (a repeated sentence is kept once, at its first occurrence), hedge-word removal, and few-shot example trimming with a note of how many were dropped. Fenced code blocks are hidden behind a placeholder before any rule runs and restored byte-for-byte, so code is never rewritten. A deterministic rule set and a keyword-retention heuristic (numbers, quoted strings, inline/fenced code, probable proper nouns, reporting exactly which ones a compression dropped) replace the idea's suggested Claude Haiku compression call and Claude Sonnet semantic-equivalence check, so results are free, offline, and reproducible. Token counts are the characters/4 approximation providers themselves cite for English text, not a real tokenizer. Live token/cost estimate, word-level diff, per-section rule breakdown, copy-compressed and JSON-template export. 76 vitest tests, 100% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, runner verified the page returns 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session as a static, fully client-side web app rather than the idea's local CLI, so it deploys with zero install: you drop in (or paste) MCP configs (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf/Cline, VS Code mcp.json and settings, Claude Code ~/.claude.json and .mcp.json), Claude Code settings.json permissions, Chrome/Edge extension manifest.json files, and VS Code extension package.json files, and nothing is uploaded. Each tool gets a 0-100 blast-radius score across filesystem, shell/code exec, network egress, credentials, and browser data, with a plain-English explanation and the exact config evidence per capability. Known MCP servers are matched by launch command (filesystem path args classified as root/home/sensitive/scoped; Docker mounts, --privileged, and the Docker socket scored; remote servers by host with plain HTTP flagged); an unrecognized local server is scored as full-privilege code, not as safe. Hygiene findings cover plaintext secrets (env, headers, connection strings in args, known token prefixes; masked in output), unpinned npx/uvx packages and :latest images, auto-approved tools, bypassPermissions, enableAllProjectMcpServers, MV2, unsafe-eval CSP, and off-store update URLs. Downloadable self-contained HTML report. Limitation: it scores declared config only, never a server's code. 95 vitest tests, >99% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green. First deploy failed because the root .gitignore excludes lockfiles; after force-adding package-lock.json the GitHub Actions deploy workflow created the site and the runner verified the page.

Built in one session, fully client-side: pick or drop a project folder and the browser walks it (File System Access API in Chromium, webkitdirectory input and drag-and-drop elsewhere; names and sizes only, nothing uploaded), draws a hand-written squarified treemap with click-to-zoom and breadcrumbs colored by ten categories (location before extension, so a PNG in node_modules is a dependency), and runs 19 ordered ecosystem-aware junk rules (venv via pyvenv.cfg, conda, __pycache__, egg-info, node_modules, .next, Maven target/ only next to a pom.xml, Gradle build/, .NET bin/obj only next to a .csproj, Unity Library/Temp/Build only under Assets+ProjectSettings, C/CMake objects, Cargo target, generic dist/build, coverage, logs, .DS_Store, editor swap files, Terraform, secrets, files over 10 MB). Each file counts toward its first matching rule; untick findings to refine a before/after estimate and the .gitignore block or unified diff against the existing .gitignore; standalone HTML report download; a deterministic 8,847-file synthetic student repo as the demo (?sample). History mode (large blobs only in git history plus the filter-repo command) was left out as beyond Weekend size. 40 vitest tests, 100% statement coverage on core; lint/typecheck/build green; end-to-end verified in headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, page verified 200 and the sample rendered in headless Chromium), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: a six-rung ladder (Caesar, affine, Vigenere, columnar transposition, monoalphabetic substitution, homophonic over two-digit symbols with frequency-proportional symbol counts) where each rung unlocks after a correct solve. The workbench has letter, bigram and trigram frequencies against English baselines, index of coincidence for periods 1-12 with English/random reference lines, a Kasiski table (repeated trigrams, distances, and which periods divide them), a per-column chart for Vigenere, symbol histograms and repeated pairs for homophonic, and keyboard-only substitution and symbol boards that decrypt live; every chart is an SVG with a data table for screen readers. Hints come from an instructor-set budget and each reveals one key fragment. The idea's LLM debrief is a deterministic solver per cipher (chi-squared over all shifts or all 312 affine keys, Kasiski vs IC then per-column Caesar, every read order for up to 7 columns then swap hill-climbing, frequency-seeded trigram hill-climb for substitution, simulated annealing with a letter-histogram penalty for homophonic) whose step log is shown beside the student's path with its accuracy, its own confidence, and the first letters it got wrong; the trigram model is trained on about 11k letters of 14 bundled public-domain passages, so confidence is discounted on short texts. Supabase auth and rosters are replaced by an instructor ladder builder that encodes the whole assignment in the URL fragment, localStorage progress with JSON export, and a dashboard that reads any number of exports (current rung, time per rung, hints, tools used, per-rung median time). 65 vitest tests, 100% statement coverage on the core; lint/typecheck/build green; end-to-end verified in headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try; the runner's immediate check hit a 404 during DNS propagation, the page returned 200 within a minute and the live index.html matches the local build), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: quote-or-refuse course Q&A where every answer is a passage from the instructor's syllabus, specs or policies (PDF via pdf.js, Markdown or text), verified word for word after whitespace/typography folding (labelled relaxations: capitalization, in-order ellipsis) and highlighted in a side-by-side viewer; otherwise 'Not stated in the course documents' plus the question words the documents never use. The idea's Claude Haiku proposer is a deterministic BM25 sentence retriever with heading context, a course-logistics synonym table and numbered-item matching ('lab 3' finds 'labs 1 to 4', 'lab 6' finds 'lab 5 onward', a passage naming other lab numbers cannot answer), so there is no API key or server. A Check-a-quote mode verifies quotes pasted from a chatbot and word-diffs altered ones against the closest passage. Questions and 'did not answer' feedback are logged per browser, exported as JSON, and merged into an instructor gap report (by week, similar wording, missing words; Markdown/CSV). Course packs travel deflated in the URL fragment or as hosted JSON (?pack=). 91 vitest tests, 99.7% statement coverage on the core; lint/typecheck/build green; end-to-end verified in headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths, including a Chromium-printed two-page PDF. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow from the feature branch; the live index.html references the same bundle as the local build.

Built in one session, fully client-side: students write dispatch(car, state) in JavaScript and it runs in a Web Worker (killed after 8 s) against seeded scenarios in an animated SVG building with two to three cars, door time and capacity. Six built-in scenarios (textbook disk trace, morning rush, lunch spike, starvation trap, quiet evening, cylinder storm) plus instructor JSON with deterministic generators (up-peak, down-peak, lunch, interfloor) and a hidden flag for grading; disk scenarios are kind: disk. Metrics: mean, p95 and max wait (unserved count until max time), mean ride, energy (floors travelled = head movement), finish time, stops, served/unserved. Side-by-side compare replays two policies in sync; the disk view redraws the same run as cylinder across, time down. Six presets (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, LOOK, C-LOOK, zoned LOOK) as readable source; tests pin the textbook head-movement numbers 640/236/236/208/326. Supabase replaced by a localStorage leaderboard (names, scores, policy hash only) with CSV/JSON export and import, and share links that deflate the policy and scenario into the URL fragment. Cars go straight to the floor the policy names (no en-route stops), which keeps the model identical to disk scheduling. 53 vitest tests, 100% statement coverage on core; lint/typecheck/build green; verified in headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, runner verified 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: drag to paint mines on a 4x4 to 40x40 canvas grid, pick a safe opening (or let Best start try up to 80 openings in a Web Worker), and a four-tier solver plays the board from that opening without ever guessing: single-cell rules, pairwise overlap bounds (1-2 and subset patterns), exhaustive per-component frontier enumeration with a 250k-node budget, then the global mine count (which is what clears a walled box). Solved means every safe cell is opened; the solver runs against the real board and throws if it ever flags a safe cell or opens a mine, swept over 120 random boards in tests. Stuck cells are amber, cells no number reaches are pale, Layout A/B overlays two mine placements for the smallest ambiguous region that both fit every visible number, and a worker ranks single-cell edits near the trouble (guess-free first, then cells uncovered, then easier tier). A slider replays the deduction step by step; the difficulty meter reports the hardest tier used. Boards travel in the URL fragment (about 270 characters at 40x40) and open in a play mode with flags, long-press, chording and a reveal of the drawing on a win. Vanilla TypeScript and canvas instead of the suggested React/Tailwind. Limitation: fixes are single-cell edits only, so some boards need fixing one step at a time. 40 vitest tests, 99.9% statement coverage on core; lint/typecheck/build green; verified in headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, runner verified 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side: a Web Worker enumerates every reachable state of Towers of Hanoi (1-8 disks, 3-5 pegs), sliding tiles up to the 8-puzzle (181,440 states, farthest start at 31 moves), the classic Klotski (13,011 states with same-shape pieces merged and mirror reduction, 25,955 without; 116 single-step moves optimal) and Rush Hour boards, then a second BFS from the goals gives exact distance-to-goal for every state. Layered layout (column = distance from start, barycentre-ordered within columns) or radial, drawn on a 2D canvas with an offscreen edge cache; colour by distance, heuristic value or heuristic error; hover previews the state, click to inspect or make it the new start. BFS, DFS, graph-variant IDDFS, greedy and A* run as steppable searches with expanded/frontier/peak-memory/generated counters, all testing the goal at expansion for fair comparison, and a run table compares them on one atlas. Students write the body of a JavaScript heuristic; the checker evaluates it on every state and reports admissibility (overestimate count and worst margin), consistency, h(goal)=0 and informedness, outlining violations on the atlas. Presets include a deliberately inadmissible Manhattan x2 and an admissible-but-inconsistent Hanoi heuristic. Instructors export puzzle + algorithm + expansion target as a base64url challenge link that judges the student's run. Canvas 2D replaces the suggested Sigma.js/regl; no LLM anywhere. Space capped at 400k states. 65 vitest tests, 99.6% statement coverage on core; lint/typecheck/build green; verified in headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow (site created first try, runner verified 200), siteId pinned afterward.

Built in one session, fully client-side in vanilla TypeScript + SVG (no React/Tailwind). The Enigma I core reproduces the textbook vectors, the double step, and the 1930 instruction-manual message with ring settings, plugboard and UKW-A. Every keypress returns its nine-hop signal path, drawn through plugboard, rotors and reflector with the full wiring faint behind it; cycle decompositions of each rotor and of the whole stack are shown. Crib sliding marks impossible offsets (letter enciphering to itself), the menu graph gets a fundamental cycle basis with loops coloured, and the Bombe runs in a Web Worker over up to 60 rotor orders x 17,576 positions: loops through the test letter are a fixed-point prefilter on the composed scramblers (Turing's test), survivors are propagated with Welchman's diagonal board, and a checking-machine pass rejects stops whose implied plugs conflict or whose other menu components die. The full search takes about a second in the browser (precomputed per-rotor-order scrambler tables, generation-tagged visited buffers). A tracer follows one hypothesis implication by implication, with the diagonal board switchable off. Challenge links carry ciphertext, crib and lightly scrambled settings; the generator guarantees no middle-rotor turnover inside the crib and the page grades a pasted decryption letter by letter. Stops report core positions at ring A, so random-ring challenges decrypt through the crib and drift after a turnover. 55 vitest tests, 98.8% statement coverage; lint/typecheck/build green. Deployed by the auto-discovering GitHub Actions deploy workflow to Netlify.

Built in one session, fully client-side: a word-accurate CS:APP-style heap (boundary tags, prologue/epilogue, padding, pred/succ pointers in free payloads) replaying malloc-lab or C-style traces under first/next/best/worst fit on implicit, explicit or segregated lists with immediate, deferred or no coalescing, realloc with keep/shrink/absorb/move, and policy switches mid-replay. Compare tab runs eight policies on the same trace with utilization, fragmentation and search-cost charts; the quiz generator reads answers off the simulator and exports Markdown or a Canvas QTI zip (dependency-free zip writer); diff mode finds the first op where a student allocator's addresses diverge and flags misalignment, overlap and bounds bugs. React/Tailwind/Recharts/Supabase replaced by plain TypeScript, SVG and URL share links. Fixed arena with no sbrk, so malloc-lab utilization scoring is not reproduced. 57 vitest tests, 99.1% stmt coverage.

Built in one session, fully client-side in vanilla TypeScript and canvas: a simplified AGC Executive with priorities and the real pools of 7 core sets and 5 VAC areas runs SERVICER, landing radar, downlink, DSKY refresh and the crew's V16N68 monitor every 2 s. A radar cycle-steal slider makes low-priority jobs starve and keep their slots until a request fails and 1202 (or 1201 when VAC areas run out first) fires from real exhaustion; the restart flushes everything and re-establishes only restart-protected jobs at their last phase, so guidance keeps flying a 1D descent. At the default 15% steal with the monitor on it lands with five alarms; a halt-on-overflow Executive aborts at the first and naive round-robin misses guidance deadlines and lands hard. Compare tab with guidance timelines and a steal sweep, DSKY panel, Apollo 11 timeline tab, share links. Job sizes are invented to match the real load level, not taken from Luminary. 36 vitest tests, 100% statement coverage on the core. Deployed via the GitHub Actions deploy workflow, siteId pinned afterward.
